calls.title: Chaos + GrowthBook
calls.summary: Chaos is focusing on maturing its experimentation capabilities to gain insights into user behavior and optimize conversion rates. Jake Wallace emphasized the importance of full funnel attribution to address measurement gaps and cater to multiple user types, including B2B, B2C, and the education sector. Their past experimentation leaned more towards B2B thinking, yet user flows resemble B2C. The integration of GrowthBook will facilitate better data access and experimentation, building upon the foundational tools currently in use. With traffic around 1 million visits, Chaos is well-positioned for statistically valid experiments. The team plans to commence experimentation soon, pending documentation review and internal discussions for proving concepts.
calls.keywords: A/B Testing, Feature Flags, Experimentation, Roketta CMS, Core Web Vitals, Product Analytics
calls.action_items:
**Christian Liebenow**
Send detailed documentation on flicker avoidance, latency minimization, core web vitals impact, and GDPR cookie compliance to Bozhidar Kamenski (50:00)
Provide detailed integration approaches for GrowthBook with Roketta CMS, especially cache and edge handling (50:00)

**Bozhidar Kamenski**
Review GrowthBook documentation on integration and compliance and send any additional technical questions following review (50:20)

**Jake Wallace**
Coordinate internal review of GrowthBook materials and sync with team to determine next steps for proof of concept or initial experimentation launch (51:40)

**Logan Bates**
Provide demo and detailed answers regarding product analytics, experiment setup, and feature flagging capabilities (00:00)

calls.title: Chaos + GrowthBook
calls.summary: The discussion emphasized creating a reliable testing foundation before scaling experimentation efforts, specifically through early organic traffic tests that identified and fixed bugs. Concerns about data integrity from past AB testing tools led to the selection of GrowthBook for accurate user flow tracking. Data architecture improvements were highlighted, necessitating SQL skills for detailed metric breakdowns. The need for efficient query costs in BigQuery was discussed, with best practices for caching and materialized views. The potential benefits of upgrading to an Enterprise plan were evaluated, contingent on stabilizing data setup. Additionally, measures for managing metrics post-experiment were reviewed, advocating for precomputed metrics to optimize costs, and overall communication strategies were solidified for ongoing collaboration.
calls.keywords: GrowthBook, fact tables, slicing, experiment tracking, enterprise plan, data warehouse
